The 'AI Omnibus' (Digital Omnibus on AI) amending Regulation 2024/1689 was adopted 19 November 2025, reached political agreement between Council and Parliament on 7 May 2026, and entered into force on 27 July 2026.
Under the AI Omnibus amendment, the obligations for high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III now apply starting 2 December 2027, rather than 2 August 2026.
Obligations for high-risk AI systems embedded in regulated products listed in Annex I (machinery, toys, lifts, etc., under Union harmonisation legislation) now apply from 2 August 2028.
The consolidated legal text of Article 113 of Regulation 2024/1689 provides that Chapter III, Sections 1, 2 and 3 (except Article 6(5)) shall apply from 2 December 2027.
The amending instrument is identified as Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, part of the Digital Omnibus on AI, which moved the Annex III deadline from 2 August 2026 to 2 December 2027.

The Commission had proposed adjusting the timeline for high-risk AI rules by up to 16 months so that the rules would start to apply once the Commission confirmed that needed standards and compliance tools were available, rather than fixing a specific calendar date.

Article 111(2) of the consolidated Regulation provides that for certain high-risk AI systems already placed on the market, the Regulation applies only if, after the 'date of application of Chapter III referred to in Article 113', those systems undergo significant design changes.
Providers and deployers of high-risk AI systems intended for use by public authorities must take necessary steps to comply regardless of the general transitional provisions.

Standards required for high-risk AI compliance were delayed, which the Commission and digital strategy office cited as jeopardizing the original 2 August 2026 entry into application and justifying the extension to 2 December 2027 (and 2 August 2028 for Annex I systems).

# When Do Obligations for High-Risk AI Systems Under Annex III of the EU AI Act Apply?

## Executive Summary
Annex III high-risk AI system obligations were originally scheduled to apply from 2 August 2026 under the EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689) as enacted (high confidence). However, the "AI Omnibus" amendment, which entered into force on 27 July 2026, pushed this deadline to **2 December 2027** (high confidence). A separate, later deadline of 2 August 2028 applies to high-risk AI systems embedded in regulated products under Annex I (high confidence).

## Key Findings

### Original Timeline (As Enacted)
Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 entered into force on 1 August 2024, and as originally drafted, obligations in Chapter III, Sections 1–3, governing high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III, were scheduled to apply from 2 August 2026—36 months after entry into force (high confidence) ([European Parliament](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/topics/en/article/20230601STO93804/eu-ai-act-first-regulation-on-artificial-intelligence); [Artificial Intelligence Act EU](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/implementation-timeline); [McKenna Consultants](https://www.mckennaconsultants.com/eu-ai-act-high-risk-compliance-a-technical-readiness-guide-for-august-2026)).

### The AI Omnibus Amendment
The Digital Omnibus on AI was adopted on 19 November 2025, reached political agreement between the Council and Parliament on 7 May 2026, and entered into force on 27 July 2026 (high confidence) ([European Commission](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai); [Council of the EU](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules)). Under this amendment, Annex III high-risk AI obligations now apply starting **2 December 2027**, rather than the original 2 August 2026 date (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation); [European Commission](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force); [AnnexOps](https://annexops.com/eu-ai-act-annex-iii-deadline-2027)).

A separate deadline of **2 August 2028** applies to high-risk AI systems embedded in regulated products under Annex I (e.g., machinery, toys, lifts, subject to Union harmonisation legislation) (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation); [European Commission](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/faqs/navigating-ai-act)).

### Rationale for the Delay
The Commission cited delays in the development of standards required for high-risk AI compliance as jeopardizing the original 2 August 2026 date, justifying the extension (medium confidence) ([European Commission](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/faqs/navigating-ai-act)). Notably, the Commission's original proposal envisioned a conditional mechanism—tying the start of obligations to confirmation that necessary standards and compliance tools were available—rather than a fixed calendar date, though the final adopted text settled on 2 December 2027 (medium confidence) ([Council of the EU](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules)).

### Legal Text and Exceptions
The consolidated legal text (Article 113) states that Chapter III, Sections 1, 2, and 3 (except Article 6(5)) apply from 2 December 2027 (low confidence, single source) ([AI Act Law](https://ai-act-law.eu/article/113)). The amending instrument is reportedly Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (low confidence) ([AnnexOps](https://annexops.com/eu-ai-act-annex-iii-deadline-2027); [EU AI Compass](https://euaicompass.com/timeline.html)). Article 111(2) provides that for certain high-risk AI systems already placed on the market, the Regulation applies only if those systems undergo significant design changes after the Article 113 application date (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727); [AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-111)). Providers and deployers of high-risk AI systems intended for use by public authorities must comply regardless of these general transitional provisions (high confidence) (same sources).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
Several sources—particularly undated legal-analysis and news-blog pieces—continue to cite 2 August 2026 as the operative deadline, reflecting information that predates the AI Omnibus amendment ([Cloud Security Alliance](https://labs.cloudsecurityalliance.org/research/csa-research-note-eu-ai-act-high-risk-compliance-deadline-20); [Responsible AI Labs](https://responsibleailabs.ai/knowledge-hub/articles/eu-ai-act-august-2026-compliance)) versus official EU sources confirming the 2 December 2027 date ([European Commission](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force)). One source describing a 36-month timeline from entry into force would imply an August 2027 date, inconsistent with both the original and amended deadlines, suggesting imprecision ([European Parliament](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/topics/en/article/20230601STO93804/eu-ai-act-first-regulation-on-artificial-intelligence)). Additionally, the Council's description of a conditional, standards-based mechanism in the Commission's proposal differs from the fixed calendar date in the final adopted text, suggesting the mechanism may have been simplified during negotiation. The claims citing Article 113's text and Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 are each flagged as **low confidence**, resting on single, non-official sources.

## Knowledge Gaps
It remains unclear whether the final AI Omnibus regulation retains any conditional mechanism that could further delay 2 December 2027, or whether this is now a fixed deadline. The precise official citation and full text of the amending regulation (purportedly 2026/1744) require verification. How the delay interacts with Article 6(5) classification guidance, and what transitional/grandfathering provisions apply to systems placed on the market before 2 August 2026, also remain open questions.

## Key Findings

### Original Timeline (As Enacted)
Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 entered into force on 1 August 2024, and as originally drafted, obligations in Chapter III, Sections 1–3, governing high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III, were scheduled to apply from 2 August 2026—36 months after entry into force (high confidence) ([European Parliament](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/topics/en/article/20230601STO93804/eu-ai-act-first-regulation-on-artificial-intelligence); [Artificial Intelligence Act EU](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/implementation-timeline); [McKenna Consultants](https://www.mckennaconsultants.com/eu-ai-act-high-risk-compliance-a-technical-readiness-guide-for-august-2026)).

### The AI Omnibus Amendment
The Digital Omnibus on AI was adopted on 19 November 2025, reached political agreement between the Council and Parliament on 7 May 2026, and entered into force on 27 July 2026 (high confidence) ([European Commission](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai); [Council of the EU](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules)). Under this amendment, Annex III high-risk AI obligations now apply starting **2 December 2027**, rather than the original 2 August 2026 date (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation); [European Commission](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force); [AnnexOps](https://annexops.com/eu-ai-act-annex-iii-deadline-2027)).

A separate deadline of **2 August 2028** applies to high-risk AI systems embedded in regulated products under Annex I (e.g., machinery, toys, lifts, subject to Union harmonisation legislation) (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation); [European Commission](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/faqs/navigating-ai-act)).

### Rationale for the Delay
The Commission cited delays in the development of standards required for high-risk AI compliance as jeopardizing the original 2 August 2026 date, justifying the extension (medium confidence) ([European Commission](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/faqs/navigating-ai-act)). Notably, the Commission's original proposal envisioned a conditional mechanism—tying the start of obligations to confirmation that necessary standards and compliance tools were available—rather than a fixed calendar date, though the final adopted text settled on 2 December 2027 (medium confidence) ([Council of the EU](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules)).

### Legal Text and Exceptions
The consolidated legal text (Article 113) states that Chapter III, Sections 1, 2, and 3 (except Article 6(5)) apply from 2 December 2027 (low confidence, single source) ([AI Act Law](https://ai-act-law.eu/article/113)). The amending instrument is reportedly Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (low confidence) ([AnnexOps](https://annexops.com/eu-ai-act-annex-iii-deadline-2027); [EU AI Compass](https://euaicompass.com/timeline.html)). Article 111(2) provides that for certain high-risk AI systems already placed on the market, the Regulation applies only if those systems undergo significant design changes after the Article 113 application date (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727); [AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-111)). Providers and deployers of high-risk AI systems intended for use by public authorities must comply regardless of these general transitional provisions (high confidence) (same sources).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
Several sources—particularly undated legal-analysis and news-blog pieces—continue to cite 2 August 2026 as the operative deadline, reflecting information that predates the AI Omnibus amendment ([Cloud Security Alliance](https://labs.cloudsecurityalliance.org/research/csa-research-note-eu-ai-act-high-risk-compliance-deadline-20); [Responsible AI Labs](https://responsibleailabs.ai/knowledge-hub/articles/eu-ai-act-august-2026-compliance)) versus official EU sources confirming the 2 December 2027 date ([European Commission](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force)). One source describing a 36-month timeline from entry into force would imply an August 2027 date, inconsistent with both the original and amended deadlines, suggesting imprecision ([European Parliament](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/topics/en/article/20230601STO93804/eu-ai-act-first-regulation-on-artificial-intelligence)). Additionally, the Council's description of a conditional, standards-based mechanism in the Commission's proposal differs from the fixed calendar date in the final adopted text, suggesting the mechanism may have been simplified during negotiation. The claims citing Article 113's text and Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 are each flagged as **low confidence**, resting on single, non-official sources.

## Knowledge Gaps
It remains unclear whether the final AI Omnibus regulation retains any conditional mechanism that could further delay 2 December 2027, or whether this is now a fixed deadline. The precise official citation and full text of the amending regulation (purportedly 2026/1744) require verification. How the delay interacts with Article 6(5) classification guidance, and what transitional/grandfathering provisions apply to systems placed on the market before 2 August 2026, also remain open questions.
